answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I spent all 3 Energy and my single Spark. Ka-pow! costs 0 Energy and spends the 1 Spark I have, so it is free damage this turn: 7 to the Sludge Spinner. Then both copies of Kaboom! for 1 Energy each, 7 damage apiece. That is 21 damage into a 37 HP enemy with no Block, leaving it at 16. The last Energy went to Duck and Cover for 5 Block, which turns the telegraphed 8-damage Attack into 3 damage to my face, so I end the turn at 39/62 instead of 34/62.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: Spark Knight's Oath was the real alternative and I weighed it seriously. It costs 2 of my 3 Energy and re-prices my Attacks that do not already cost Spark to 3 Spark instead of Energy. With it down I would have 1 Energy left and 1 Spark: Ka-pow! still spends that Spark for 7, but then both Kaboom!s would want 3 Spark each and I would have 0 Spark and no way printed in this hand to make more. So the Oath turn is 7 damage and either 5 Block or nothing, versus 21 damage and 5 Block. The Oath only pays off if Spark income arrives on a later turn, and nothing on this page tells me it does. I also considered dropping Duck and Cover for nothing better and just holding it, and playing the three attacks without Block to keep a card — but there is no draw or retention text here, so an unplayed card is only worth what a future hand does with it, which the page does not show.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: It gave up the Oath entirely — I burned my only Spark on Ka-pow! this turn, so the Oath's engine, whatever it builds toward across a fight, is not started. If Spark generation exists elsewhere in Klee's deck, the correct long-game play might have been to lay the Oath early while it is cheap in tempo terms and bank Sparks; I traded that whole possibility for immediate damage I can verify. It also gave up nothing in reserve: my hand is empty at end of turn, so a nastier turn-two intent finds me with no held Block card.
answers.q4_different_intent: Yes, on the margin. Against this 8-damage Attack, Duck and Cover prevents 5 of it — real but small. If the Spinner had telegraphed a defensive or buffing intent, or a block-gaining one, I would have skipped Duck and Cover; with 3 Energy and no incoming damage the third point of Energy has no attack left to buy in this hand (Ka-pow! is already free and both Kaboom!s are cast), so I would have spent the 2 on Spark Knight's Oath instead and used the turn to set up rather than shield against nothing. If the intent had been a very large hit — enough that 5 Block was irrelevant and I was dying regardless — I would also have dropped the Block and gone pure damage, though with 42 HP against a 37 HP enemy that case does not arise here. The attack order among the three damage cards is not sensitive to intent: same total, and the enemy has no Block or aura to sequence around.
